questions.question: What causes the regular cycle of day and night on Earth?
About how long does Earth take to orbit the Sun once?
What is the main cause of Earth's seasons?
choices: Earth's axial tilt as it orbits the Sun
The Sun orbiting Earth every year

questions.question: During a solar eclipse, which object lies between Earth and the Sun?
During a lunar eclipse, which object lies between the Sun and the Moon?
What causes the Moon's visible phases?
choices: The Moon changing its actual shape
The Moon producing different amounts of light
Earth casting a shadow on it every night
Changes in how much of its sunlit half we see

questions.question: At which phase is the Moon's near side fully illuminated as viewed from Earth?
Why is it summer in the Northern Hemisphere when it is winter in the Southern Hemisphere?
choices: Each hemisphere receives summer when Earth is closest to the Sun
The hemisphere with more oceans always has winter
The Sun's energy output alternates between hemispheres
The hemispheres tilt toward and away from the Sun in opposite ways

questions.question: Why does a hemisphere tilted toward the Sun receive more heating?
choices: It generally has longer days and more direct sunlight
It moves much closer to the Sun than the other hemisphere

questions.question: Why do eclipses not occur at every new and full moon?
choices: The Moon does not orbit Earth regularly
Earth's shadow exists only once a year
The Moon's orbital plane is tilted relative to Earth's orbital plane
The Sun changes position inside the solar system

questions.question: Why does the Moon generally show the same face to Earth?
choices: Its rotation period matches its orbital period around Earth
Its far side receives no sunlight

questions.question: What is the main astronomical cause of ocean tides?
choices: Differences in the Moon's and Sun's gravitational pulls across Earth
Winds always blowing toward the equator
Earth moving closer to the Sun each evening

questions.question: When do spring tides generally occur?
choices: Around new and full moons, when Sun, Earth, and Moon align
Only when the Moon is at first quarter
Whenever the ocean surface becomes warmer

questions.question: How do neap tides compare with spring tides?
choices: They always have a greater tidal range
They occur only once per year
They have a smaller tidal range

questions.question: Why is a new moon usually difficult to see from Earth?
choices: The Moon reflects less light because its surface changes color
Earth's shadow covers the whole Moon
The Moon's sunlit side mainly faces away from Earth
The Moon is fully lit on its near side but too distant to see

questions.question: Which sequence gives the correct order of these phases after a new moon?
In June, the Northern Hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun. What season generally occurs in southern Australia?
A student claims seasons happen because Earth is much closer to the Sun in northern summer. Which fact best challenges this explanation?
choices: The two hemispheres have opposite seasons at the same time
Earth rotates from west to east

questions.question: A diagram shows Sun, Earth, and Moon in that order, nearly aligned. Which event could occur?
choices: An eclipse of the Sun by Mars

questions.question: A coastal location has unusually large differences between high and low tide near a full moon. Which explanation fits?
choices: The Moon's visible brightness directly raises ocean water
The Moon's gravitational influence disappears at full moon
The Sun's and Moon's tidal effects reinforce each other during alignment
The Sun's and Moon's tidal effects oppose each other most strongly
